plugin.name: mush_windows
plugin.author: Mark
plugin.purpose: Shared window chrome (drag/resize/min/max/close/snap) plus a Windows list

muclient.script:
local winframe = assert(loadfile(GetPluginInfo(GetPluginID(), 20) .. "winframe.lua"))()
local windows = {} -- winframe id -> { left, top, w, h, title, owner, visible } local taskbarWin = nil -- assigned in OnPluginInstall, read by the functions below
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Windows list / taskbar -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
local ROW_H = 18 local CLOSE_W = 16
-- Ordered (alphabetical by title), excluding the taskbar's own entry -- -- shared by drawing and hotspot setup so the two never drift apart, same -- pattern OertheMap.xml uses for its own control layout. local function TaskbarRows() local ids = {} for id in pairs(windows) do if id ~= taskbarWin.id then ids[#ids + 1] = id end end table.sort(ids, function(a, b) return (windows[a].title or a) < (windows[b].title or b) end)
local rows = {} for i, id in ipairs(ids) do local top = (i - 1) * ROW_H rows[#rows + 1] = { id = id, rec = windows[id], top = top, bottom = top + ROW_H } end return rows end
local function DrawTaskbar(contentW, contentH) local top0 = taskbarWin:contentTop() local rows = TaskbarRows()
if #rows == 0 then WindowText(taskbarWin.win, taskbarWin.titleFontId, "(no windows yet)", 4, top0 + 2, contentW - 4, top0 + ROW_H, 0x888888, false) return end
local closeL = contentW - CLOSE_W for _, row in ipairs(rows) do local textColour = row.rec.visible and 0xFFFFFF or 0x888888 WindowText(taskbarWin.win, taskbarWin.titleFontId, row.rec.title or row.id, 4, top0 + row.top + 2, closeL - 2, top0 + row.bottom, textColour, false) WindowText(taskbarWin.win, taskbarWin.titleFontId, "x", closeL, top0 + row.top + 2, contentW - 4, top0 + row.bottom, 0xAAAAAA, false) end end
local function TaskbarHotspots(contentW, contentH) local top0 = taskbarWin:contentTop() local closeL = contentW - CLOSE_W for _, row in ipairs(TaskbarRows()) do WindowAddHotspot(taskbarWin.win, "mw_row_" .. row.id, 0, top0 + row.top, closeL, top0 + row.bottom, "", "", "MwTaskbarRowMouseDown", "", "", "Bring to front", miniwin.cursor_hand, 0) WindowAddHotspot(taskbarWin.win, "mw_close_" .. row.id, closeL, top0 + row.top, contentW, top0 + row.bottom, "", "", "MwTaskbarCloseMouseDown", "", "", "Hide", miniwin.cursor_hand, 0) end end
-- Called on every registry write, including the ones the taskbar's OWN -- winframe instance triggers on itself (syncGeometry, throttled, during a -- live drag/resize of the taskbar's own title bar/edges). A plain -- taskbarWin:redraw() would call setupHotspots() -> WindowDeleteAllHotspots -- there too, deleting the very "zz_drag"/resize hotspot that gesture is -- currently tracked on and silently ending it after the first throttled -- tick -- the exact bug this same pattern already caused (and was fixed) -- in oerthe_map's own pan-drag, just triggered a different way here: only -- dragging the TASKBAR loops back onto itself like this; dragging some -- OTHER window's title bar only ever refreshes the taskbar's ROW LIST -- content, never its own hotspots, since the window doing the dragging -- and the window being refreshed are different windows in that case. -- Repainting content only, while a gesture owns this window, dodges that -- entirely -- correct because rows/close-buttons are laid out purely -- from contentW, which a MOVE never changes; a RESIZE's own release -- handler already does a full redraw() once the gesture itself is over. local function RefreshTaskbar() if not taskbarWin then return end if taskbarWin.dragState or taskbarWin.resizeState then taskbarWin:repaintContent() else taskbarWin:redraw() end end
function MwTaskbarRowMouseDown(flags, hotspotId) local id = hotspotId:match("^mw_row_(.+)$") local rec = id and windows[id] if rec and rec.owner then pcall(CallPlugin, rec.owner, "WinframeActivate", id) end end
function MwTaskbarCloseMouseDown(flags, hotspotId) local id = hotspotId:match("^mw_close_(.+)$") local rec = id and windows[id] if rec and rec.owner then pcall(CallPlugin, rec.owner, "WinframeHide", id) end end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Window-geometry registry, called into via CallPlugin by winframe.lua -- (running inside each CONSUMER plugin's own Lua state, including this -- plugin's own taskbar window -- see the header comment above). -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function WF_Registry_Update(id, left, top, w, h, title, owner, visible) windows[id] = { left = left, top = top, w = w, h = h, title = title, owner = owner, visible = visible } RefreshTaskbar() return true end
function WF_Registry_Remove(id) windows[id] = nil RefreshTaskbar() return true end
-- Returns every OTHER registered window's geometry (excludeId omitted) as -- one packed string: "id1:left,top,w,h|id2:left,top,w,h|...". Packed into -- a single string because CallPlugin can only return one plain value, not -- a table. Used for snapping only, so title/owner/visible aren't included. function WF_Registry_Get(excludeId) local parts = {} for id, rec in pairs(windows) do if id ~= excludeId then parts[#parts + 1] = id .. ":" .. rec.left .. "," .. rec.top .. "," .. rec.w .. "," .. rec.h end end return table.concat(parts, "|") end
function OnPluginInstall() ColourNote("orange", "", "[mush_windows] ready -- shared window chrome for other plugins in this set.")
taskbarWin = winframe.new{ id = "mush_windows_taskbar", title = "Windows", min_content_w = 90, min_content_h = ROW_H * 2, default_content_w = 150, default_content_h = ROW_H * 5, on_draw = DrawTaskbar, on_hotspots = TaskbarHotspots, } taskbarWin:show() end
-- Fallback in case the taskbar's own close button gets used and someone -- forgets it's just hidden, not gone -- wired to the wf_windows alias -- below, mirroring the inv_show/inv_hide pattern oerthe_inventory already -- uses for its own window. function WfShowWindows() taskbarWin:show() end
